brief: nameAt(x,y) names the ground, the plants, the plots, the waters and the thirteen trees — and nothing that MOVES. Point at a walker, a duck, a swan, the sweeper, a gardener with a basket, the rowboat, the concert audience or the cat, and the sill says the paving under their feet. Since #33 the living things are the most legible part of a night frame. __entities() already carries role, act and a stable id per person, and crowns[] is the pattern for hit-testing a moving thing in SCREEN space. Give the pointer the living things, with the same NAME_SETTLE hold as everything else, and let the name say what they are DOING ('someone waiting at the door', 'a swan, upending') rather than only what they are.
successLooksLike: probes/naming.mjs extended: over ten seeds, pointing at the screen position of any agent, duck, swan or the boat returns a living name at least 95% of the time and NEVER the paving, and pointing at a spot 2 cells clear of every entity still returns exactly what HEAD returns. A moving figure holds its name for NAME_SETTLE after it walks out from under the pointer, no flicker.
avoid: Hit-test in screen space against the drawn footprint (project() the feet, a box of roughly 0.9 cells) — never re-derive world geometry, and never add an R() draw: the renderer walks the seeded stream. The sill is DOM and fails quietly: assert on computed text, not on the handler having run. Do not add a new invitation for it; OFFERS[] is the queue and the naming already has its hint.
